stemMd: Why can but-2-ene have geometric isomers whereas butane cannot have corresponding stable cis/trans isomers about its central bond?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Rotation about the double bond is restricted, while ordinary single-bond rotation is relatively free.

options.label: B
options.textMd: But-2-ene has different atomic numbers in different isomers.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Geometric isomerism depends only on molecular mass.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The double bond allows completely unrestricted rotation without changing bonding.

explanationMd: The pi component of a carbon-carbon double bond restricts rotation. In but-2-ene, each double-bond carbon has two different substituents, allowing distinct cis and trans arrangements. Butane conformations interconvert by rotation about single bonds and are not corresponding configurational cis/trans isomers.

distractorRationale.c: Connectivity and substituent arrangement are decisive.
distractorRationale.b: Isomerism does not change the identities of atoms.
